name: Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation Type 3

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and histopathologic criteria for CPAM

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small cystic lesions in lung parenchyma on prenatal or postnatal imaging
Histopathologic confirmation of adenomatoid proliferation of bronchiolar-type structures without cartilage
Neonatal respiratory distress or recurrent pulmonary infections consistent with CPAM

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lung lesions on imaging plus histopathologic confirmation of adenomatoid malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires correlation of imaging and histopathology; prenatal ultrasound and CT imaging are key.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple microcystic lesions in lung parenchyma
pathognomonic.notes: Typically identified on prenatal ultrasound or neonatal imaging
Due to mass effect and impaired lung function

common.notes: Rapid breathing in neonates and infants
Due to hypoxia from impaired gas exchange

common.symptomName: Decreased breath sounds over affected lung
searchTerms: reduced breath sounds over lung area

occasional.notes: Due to mass effect from cystic lesions
Underdevelopment of lung tissue adjacent to malformation
Due to respiratory distress and poor coordination

rare.notes: Rare bleeding from abnormal lung tissue

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers unless secondary infection present
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing echogenic lung mass with microcystic appearance
Chest CT demonstrating multiple small cystic lesions replacing lung parenchyma
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology showing adenomatoid proliferation of bronchiolar structures without cartilage

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic arterial supply on imaging
Lack of communication with tracheobronchial tree
Overinflation of a pulmonary lobe without cystic lesions
Absence of microcystic structures on imaging

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation
Rapidly enlarging thoracic mass causing cardiovascular compromise
Recurrent severe pulmonary infections unresponsive to antibiotics
references: Stocker JT. Congenital pulmonary airway malformation: a new name for and a classification of congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation of the lung. Histopathology. 2002.
Langston C. New concepts in the pathology of congenital lung malformations. Semin Pediatr Surg. 2003.
Orphanet: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation type 3 (ORPHA:280847)
